findings.claim: Proposes revising the 2020 police law, closing parole loopholes for violent offenders, and reinstating proactive policing.

findings.verifier_note: The quote describes the campaign’s plan to reform the 2020 police law, close parole loopholes, and reinstate proactive policing.

findings.claim: Proposes reducing taxes by more than $2.5 billion by the fourth year, with relief focused on middle-income families.
findings.quote: Ryan Fazio will reduce taxes by over $2.5 billion by the fourth year of his administration with relief focused on income tax relief for middle-income families

findings.claim: Proposes reducing the paid-family-leave payroll tax by 0.1 percentage points, using existing program reserves and surplus.

findings.claim: On veterans’ healthcare access, his campaign says he would streamline veteran services, reduce costs and cut fees.
findings.quote: Connecticut is home to over 130,000 veterans, yet progress on veteran homelessness, healthcare access, and job training has stalled. Ryan will streamline veteran services, reduce costs, cut fees, recognize out-of-state licenses, and support employment opportunities for those who served.
findings.verifier_note: The campaign says Ryan would streamline veteran services, reduce costs, and cut fees, in a passage that also identifies veterans’ healthcare access as an issue.

findings.claim: Proposes ending or sunsetting most programs funded through the Public Benefits Charge and moving some remaining programs into the state budget process.
findings.quote: The plan would immediately end or sunset most of the more than 50 government programs hidden in the charge and move a small portion of the remaining necessary programs to the state budget process for full transparency.
findings.source_title: Ryan’s Plan to Cut Your Electricity Bills – Ryan Fazio for Governor
findings.verifier_note: The quote supports ending or sunsetting most programs in the charge and moving a small portion of remaining programs to the state budget process.
findings.original_claim: Fazio’s electricity plan would end or sunset most programs funded through the Public Benefits Charge and move some remaining programs into the state budget process.

findings.claim: His plan would limit long-term state electricity contracts to prices close to the wholesale market price.
findings.quote: Limit any long-term contract for electricity to no more than a nominal difference from the wholesale market price of electricity, protecting ratepayers from bad deals.
findings.source_title: Ryan’s Plan to Cut Your Electricity Bills – Ryan Fazio for Governor
findings.verifier_note: The quote supports limiting long-term electricity contracts to a nominal difference from the wholesale price.

findings.claim: Proposes full expensing of capital investments to encourage business investment and long-term manufacturing and industrial jobs.
findings.quote: Full expensing of capital expenditures to incentivize building factories, offices, buying machinery and plants that will lead to the long-term manufacturing and industrial jobs, around $100 million
findings.source_title: THE FAZIO TAX CUT PLAN – Ryan Fazio for Governor
findings.verifier_note: The quote supports full expensing and says it would incentivize investment and lead to long-term manufacturing and industrial jobs.
findings.original_claim: His tax plan proposes full expensing of capital investments, which it says would encourage business investment and long-term manufacturing and industrial jobs.

findings.claim: Proposes reducing spending he describes as “wasteful” and “politically oriented” by about $1 billion per year by 2031.

findings.claim: Fazio proposes that every Connecticut student be able to read by third grade, with literacy materials based on the Science of Reading.
findings.quote:
High standards for literacy education: Every Connecticut student should be able to read by 3rd grade
Materials must be oriented around proven Science of Reading
findings.source_title: LEADERSHIP ON EDUCATION FUNDING & ACCESS – Ryan Fazio for Governor
findings.verifier_note: The quote supports the third-grade reading goal and the use of materials oriented around the Science of Reading.

findings.claim: Proposes reassessing and simplifying Connecticut’s school-funding formulas and providing districts with adequate, predictable funding.
findings.quote: Connecticut currently has 10 different school funding formulas. They should be re-assessed and simplified, and districts should count on adequate, transparent, and predictable funding for their needs.
findings.source_title: LEADERSHIP ON EDUCATION FUNDING & ACCESS – Ryan Fazio for Governor
findings.verifier_note: The quote supports reassessing and simplifying school-funding formulas and says districts should count on adequate, predictable funding.
findings.original_claim: Fazio proposes reassessing and simplifying Connecticut’s school-funding formulas and providing districts with adequate, predictable funding.

Eliminate licensing fees for teachers

findings.original_claim: Fazio proposes recognizing licenses held by experienced teachers in good standing in other states and eliminating teacher licensing fees.

climate.rationale: The findings concern electricity costs and program funding but do not establish a climate-policy position matching an anchor.

crime.rationale: The 0.5 anchor fits his proposal to reinstate proactive policing and revise the 2020 police law, alongside closing parole loopholes for violent offenders.

economy.rationale: The 0.5 anchor fits his proposed tax reductions focused on middle-income families and cuts to spending he describes as wasteful.

education.rationale: The 0.0 anchor fits support for public schools alongside school choice, including charter expansion and an education tax credit for public or private settings.

healthcare.rationale: The finding concerns veterans’ service access and costs, not a position on the broader public-private coverage system in the anchors.

housing.rationale: The 0.5 anchor fits incentives for housing development, rollback of state affordable-housing requirements for more local zoning flexibility, and a cap on property-tax increases.

womens_childrens.rationale: The 0.0 anchor is the closest fit: he proposes a limited reduction in the paid-family-leave payroll tax while maintaining the program using reserves and surplus.
